correctness.rationale: A general Lie endomorphism of the affine algebra is exactly [[p,0],[r,s]] with s(1-p)=0. The Yau-twisted bracket is [e1,e2]_alpha=s e2. Direct substitution shows the Nijenhuis torsion vanishes for every 2-by-2 matrix, so the Hom-Nijenhuis condition reduces exactly to N alpha=alpha N. The endomorphism variety has 2q^2-q points. Only 0 and I are scalar; their commutants have q^4 points, while every nonscalar 2-by-2 matrix has a two-dimensional centralizer and hence q^2 commuting matrices. The packaged checker exhaustively replays all equations and counts over F2, F3, F5, and F7.

value.rationale: The two-dimensional affine Lie algebra is the unique nonabelian Lie algebra of its dimension, and all of its Lie endomorphisms give the canonical Yau-twist family. Classifying Nijenhuis operators simultaneously over the entire twist parameter space is therefore a natural complete minimal moduli problem, not an arbitrary slice. The result reveals a sharp two-point fiber jump: only the zero and identity twists have four-dimensional Nijenhuis spaces, while every other twist has dimension two, and it determines the arithmetic zeta function of the full pair variety.
